Title: Celebrating Women’s Day
NewsSummary: Working Group for Women at the Aga Khan University organised a women’s day event on March 30, 2015.
NewsContent:
​Working Group for Women at the Aga Khan University organised a women’s day event on March 30, 2015. The two-hour programme, ‘Feminine Voice of Urdu Poetry’, was aimed at celebrating the less-heard yet assertive voice of women by showcasing a blend of three fine arts – poetry, music and theatre. 

Shumaila Sadiq, BScN Year I student, was the first to share her creative thoughts with the audience. She recited a verse appreciating women for  their valuable contribution to society.

Following this was the key session for the event encompassing the experiences, approaches and themes renowned poets have touched upon with regards to women.

Anees Haroon, Resident Director of Aurat Foundation and former Chair for National Commission on Status of Women was one of the three guests who shared their poetry. Recently selected as a member of the National Commission on Human Rights for Sindh, Haroon has worked for women in Swat, Pakistan, the sight of much turmoil in the recent past. According to Haroon, the women of Swat are cognisant of their plight; however, they are firmly standing up against all odds and are fighting on multiple fronts; their children’s education being one of them. Haroon recorded their attitude as follows: 

Is raastay ka intikhab mein nay khud kiya hay 
(I myself have chosen this destiny)
Ye zeher ka piyala mein nay khud piya hay 
(I have chosen this path that leads to death)
Sisak sisak kar sadion jeenay say, apni merzi ka aik pal behtar hay 
(Living a short life of your dreams is better than living for a hundred years)

Other guest poets included Humaira Rahman and Ambreen Haseeb Amber.

Amber, who is a  PhD in Urdu and has worked as anchor-person for several social and electronic media programmes,  recited some beautiful pieces from her poetry that deal with issues faced by younger generation of women. With command over four languages – Urdu, Persian, Arabic and Sindhi – she not only writes about the delicate feelings of a woman but also about her strengths.

Rahman, the author of two acclaimed collections of poetry Intisab and Indimal, is an active member of Pakistan Immigrant Committee, New York and has been teaching Urdu as a foreign language at New York University. Her poetry draws forth what she distils from the everyday lives of women.

A theatrical performance prepared by ‘Harmony’ group comprising of students of School of Nursing and Midwifery added weight to the inspiring poetry session. Their performance themed on the injustice faced by women of all ages and from all walks of life, and was much appreciated. 

Earlier, during her welcome speech, Dr Nargis Asad, Chair, WGW said that WGW is an expanding interdisciplinary group aiming to promote a supportive environment to ensure progressive social change. It is a voluntary group of AKU employees working for greater awareness of women’s issues and concerns. “One of the mandates of WGW is to raise  awareness on women’s rights and equality. We achieve this mandate by conducting pure academic sessions or by mixing academia with fine arts like literature, music and theatre. Today’s programme is one such effort,” she said. 

As the programme ended, the audience left with Humaira Rahman’s words resonating in their minds: 

Raat ki jati aahat, subh ka narm ujala dekhay gi 
(She will see the darkness fading away and soft light slipping in)
Beenai andhi taariki ka azaala dekhay gi 
(The blind darkness will come to an end)
Meri beti jang laday gi apnay sub imkaanon ki 
(My daughter will fight for all the possibilities in life)
Dunya us men mera chehra, mera hawaala dekhay gi 
(The world would find in her; my face, my reference) ​​​
